world.title: Nigeria investigates 37 suspected miners’ deaths in custody
world.summary: At least 37 people suspected of illegal mining died on Thursday in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna, the capital of north-central Niger State, officials said. The detainees were arrested during operations on Tuesday and Wednesday. Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago said the state h
world.content: At least 37 people suspected of illegal mining died on Thursday in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna, the capital of north-central Niger State, officials said. The detainees were arrested during operations on Tuesday and Wednesday. Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago said the state had formed an inquiry committee, declared three days of mourning and postponed the start of campaigning for January elections. The cause of death remains undetermined. The NSCDC said it suspected a disease outbreak and sent the bodies to General Hospital, Minna, for examination, while an intelligence report cited overcrowding and poor ventilation. Survivor Dauda Shehu told the Associated Press that 65 detainees were held in a poorly ventilated cell and struggled to breathe; the NSCDC said claims linking the deaths to a specific disease required medical and laboratory confirmation.

world.title: Swedish PM Kristersson resigns after left bloc wins election
world.summary: Sweden’s centre-right Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson resigned on Thursday after the final count from the Sept. 13 parliamentary election gave a four-party centre-left opposition bloc 176 of the Riksdag’s 349 seats, compared with 173 for the governing alliance and its Sweden Democrat supporters. The result puts Social D
world.content: Sweden’s centre-right Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson resigned on Thursday after the final count from the Sept. 13 parliamentary election gave a four-party centre-left opposition bloc 176 of the Riksdag’s 349 seats, compared with 173 for the governing alliance and its Sweden Democrat supporters. The result puts Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson in position to try to return as prime minister, a post she lost in 2022, but she must negotiate with parties whose demands conflict. Andersson’s Social Democrats must negotiate with the Left Party, Greens and Centre Party. The Centre Party has said it will not support a government that gives cabinet posts to the Left Party, while the Left Party has demanded direct representation. Sweden’s parliamentary speaker, Andreas Norlén, will lead consultations with party leaders while Kristersson’s government remains in a caretaker role. The final margin between the two blocs was 50,359 votes, and the Sweden Democrats fell to third place after losing support from 2022.
world.image_alt: Swedish PM Kristersson resigns after left bloc wins election

world.title: President Trump weighs renewed large-scale strikes against Iran
world.summary: President Donald Trump said he faces a major decision on whether to resume large-scale attacks against Iran and did not rule out an assault aimed at destroying the Iranian regime. He told Axios that “anything could happen,” while also saying Iran wants a deal and that Washington has been in direct contact with Tehran.
world.content: President Donald Trump said he faces a major decision on whether to resume large-scale attacks against Iran and did not rule out an assault aimed at destroying the Iranian regime. He told Axios that “anything could happen,” while also saying Iran wants a deal and that Washington has been in direct contact with Tehran. The conflict began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28 and has continued for nearly seven months, with Iran retaliating against Israel and US bases as fighting spread across the region. Trump is expected to meet leaders or senior officials from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman in New York on September 22 during the UN General Assembly. He said he wants their assessment before deciding whether to pursue another diplomatic effort or intensify military operations. Reports said regional support would be important if Washington resumes major strikes. His senior adviser Massad Boulos told Euronews that Trump is determined to end the war soon but gave no timeline.
world.image_alt: President Trump weighs renewed large-scale strikes against Iran

world.title: Bolivian researchers identify new wild cat species Leopardus tilcayo
world.summary: Scientists have formally identified Leopardus tilcayo, a previously unrecognized wild-cat species living in Bolivia’s mountainous Yungas cloud forests. Known locally as the tilcayo, the animal belongs to the tiger-cat group, measures about 46 centimeters long and weighs about 1.4 kilograms. Researchers published its de
world.content: Scientists have formally identified Leopardus tilcayo, a previously unrecognized wild-cat species living in Bolivia’s mountainous Yungas cloud forests. Known locally as the tilcayo, the animal belongs to the tiger-cat group, measures about 46 centimeters long and weighs about 1.4 kilograms. Researchers published its description in Current Biology, marking the first formal naming and description of a living feline species in more than a century. An international team used genetic material from living animals, museum specimens and 38 cats sampled across South America to distinguish the tilcayo from closely related tiger cats. The study found that the group contains five distinct species and that the tilcayo lineage separated from other tiger cats about 1.4 million years ago. Researchers said the species’ wild population remains unknown and that its Yungas habitat faces deforestation, agricultural expansion, fires and mining.
world.image_alt: Bolivian researchers identify new wild cat species Leopardus tilcayo

world.title: Trump says US-Poland base talks make major progress
world.summary: President Donald Trump said Sept. 17 that Washington and Warsaw had made “major progress” toward establishing a permanent U.S. Army base in Poland and that its location could be announced soon. Trump credited Polish President Karol Nawrocki and called the prospective base a historic step for the U.S.-Polish alliance. N
world.content: President Donald Trump said Sept. 17 that Washington and Warsaw had made “major progress” toward establishing a permanent U.S. Army base in Poland and that its location could be announced soon. Trump credited Polish President Karol Nawrocki and called the prospective base a historic step for the U.S.-Polish alliance. Nawrocki said Poland was ready to continue strengthening defense cooperation and would seek the best possible site for the facility. The announcement followed Warsaw’s disclosure in August that it was holding talks with Washington over a permanent U.S. presence, but no final basing decision has been publicly documented. Poland currently hosts nearly 10,000 U.S. troops, mostly on a rotational basis, while the Trump administration is conducting a formal review of American forces in Europe. Polish officials said initial discussions had been completed, and further talks took place in Warsaw on Sept. 10.
world.image_alt: Trump says US-Poland base talks make major progress

world.title: Russia and China veto U.S. bid to extend Iran sanctions monitoring
world.summary: Russia and China vetoed a U.S.-drafted United Nations Security Council resolution on September 17 that would have extended for one year the mandate of an independent panel monitoring sanctions on Iran. The resolution received 11 votes in favor, while Russia and China voted against it and Pakistan and Somalia abstained.
world.content: Russia and China vetoed a U.S.-drafted United Nations Security Council resolution on September 17 that would have extended for one year the mandate of an independent panel monitoring sanctions on Iran. The resolution received 11 votes in favor, while Russia and China voted against it and Pakistan and Somalia abstained. The two vetoes blocked adoption despite majority support for the measure. The veto blocked renewal of the panel’s authorization, which was due to expire on September 26, but did not lift the sanctions themselves. The measures remain in effect amid a dispute over the nuclear agreement’s snapback mechanism and include freezing Iranian assets abroad, restricting arms transactions with Tehran and penalizing the development of Iran’s ballistic-missile program. The Security Council had operated without an active expert group for about a year because members could not agree on appointments.
world.image_alt: Russia and China veto U.S. bid to extend Iran sanctions monitoring

world.title: Houthis seize Red Sea coast as Yemen war escalates
world.summary: Iran-backed Houthi forces and Yemen’s Saudi-supported government exchanged strikes as fighting intensified across western Yemen and near the Saudi border. The Houthis advanced along the Red Sea coast, captured the port city of Mokha and nearby islands, and took positions around the Bab al-Mandab strait. Government forc
world.content: Iran-backed Houthi forces and Yemen’s Saudi-supported government exchanged strikes as fighting intensified across western Yemen and near the Saudi border. The Houthis advanced along the Red Sea coast, captured the port city of Mokha and nearby islands, and took positions around the Bab al-Mandab strait. Government forces reported clashes in Taiz, Lahj and Al Jawf and an advance toward the oil-rich Marib region. Saudi Arabia said debris from an intercepted Houthi drone killed a Yemeni resident in Taif and wounded two others. The Houthis denied Saudi accusations that they targeted Mecca and said Saudi strikes killed civilians and hit telecommunications infrastructure in Taiz. The latest fighting has displaced an estimated 125,000 people, with some Yemenis fleeing by boat across the Red Sea to Djibouti. Houthi-controlled media reported casualties from Saudi and government strikes, while Yemen’s government reported losses among its forces; the figures could not be independently reconciled. The escalation has threatened Saudi oil shipments and contributed to higher global fuel prices. Bab al-Mandab is a key alternative route following disruption around the Strait of Hormuz.
world.image_alt: Houthis seize Red Sea coast as Yemen war escalates

world.title: Canada backs EU associate membership plan despite Trump tariff threat
world.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney endorsed the European Union’s proposal for Canada to become the bloc’s first “associate member” in a speech to the European Parliament in Strasbourg on Sept. 17. Carney said Canada and Europe should deepen cooperation on defence, critical minerals, energy, artificial intelligence, sp
world.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney endorsed the European Union’s proposal for Canada to become the bloc’s first “associate member” in a speech to the European Parliament in Strasbourg on Sept. 17. Carney said Canada and Europe should deepen cooperation on defence, critical minerals, energy, artificial intelligence, space, research, financial services and youth exchanges that would allow young people to live, work and study across the Atlantic. He said Canada was not seeking full EU membership or a new power bloc, but a partnership to protect sovereignty, open markets and democratic institutions. The proposal's legal details remain undefined: EU treaties contain no associate-member status, and any arrangement would require approval from all 27 EU member states. President Donald Trump called the idea “laughable” and said the United States could impose “very serious tariffs” or stop trading with Europe if he considered it hostile. Carney responded that Canada would independently decide which international agreements to pursue.
world.image_alt: Canada backs EU associate membership plan despite Trump tariff threat

business.title: Tata Sons backs IPO, five-year extension for Chandrasekaran
business.summary: Tata Sons, the holding company of India’s Tata conglomerate, has approved preparations for a public listing and backed Executive Chairman N. Chandrasekaran for a further five-year term. The decision reverses Chandrasekaran’s announcement last month that he would not seek reappointment when his current tenure ends on Fe
business.content: Tata Sons, the holding company of India’s Tata conglomerate, has approved preparations for a public listing and backed Executive Chairman N. Chandrasekaran for a further five-year term. The decision reverses Chandrasekaran’s announcement last month that he would not seek reappointment when his current tenure ends on February 20, 2027. The board’s 4-1 decision followed the Reserve Bank of India’s rejection of Tata Sons’ request to surrender its core investment company registration, reviving requirements for upper-layer non-bank finance companies, including a potential listing. The decisions widened a dispute with Tata Trusts, which collectively owns about 66% of Tata Sons. Trusts chairman Noel Tata voted against Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, called the decision illegal and opposed an immediate listing. The Shapoorji Pallonji Group, which owns about 18.4%, supported taking the holding company public and proposed selling part of its stake for at least ₹25,000 crore. Tata Trusts has said the board should examine alternatives to a listing and has challenged the validity of the reappointment ahead of shareholder and regulatory steps.
business.image_alt: Tata Sons backs IPO, five-year extension for Chandrasekaran

business.title: US mortgage rates climb near 7%, pressuring housing market
business.summary: The average U.S. rate for a 30-year fixed mortgage rose to 6.95% this week from 6.76% the previous week, marking a fourth consecutive weekly increase and the highest level since January 2025. The increase came a day after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates amid persistent inflation. Higher rates add to monthly b
business.content: The average U.S. rate for a 30-year fixed mortgage rose to 6.95% this week from 6.76% the previous week, marking a fourth consecutive weekly increase and the highest level since January 2025. The increase came a day after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates amid persistent inflation. Higher rates add to monthly borrowing costs and reduce buyers’ purchasing power. Mortgage applications to buy homes fell 19% from a year earlier last week, while refinancing applications dropped 65%. Pending home sales rose 0.3% in the latest monthly data, but the number of homes under contract remained below last year’s level. August data also showed declines in housing permits, starts and completions, according to the U.S. Census Bureau and the Department of Housing and Urban Development.
business.image_alt: US mortgage rates climb near 7%, pressuring housing market

business.title: Fed raises rates as Warsh signals further hikes
business.summary: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest-rate target by a quarter percentage point on Sept. 16, to 3.75%-4.00% from 3.50%-3.75%, marking its first increase since July 2023. All 12 voting members of the Federal Open Market Committee backed the decision, citing inflation above the Fed’s 2% goal, a strengthening
business.content: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest-rate target by a quarter percentage point on Sept. 16, to 3.75%-4.00% from 3.50%-3.75%, marking its first increase since July 2023. All 12 voting members of the Federal Open Market Committee backed the decision, citing inflation above the Fed’s 2% goal, a strengthening economy and renewed energy-price pressure linked to fighting involving Iran. The Fed’s projections point to at least one more increase before the end of 2026: 16 of 18 policymakers anticipated another quarter-point hike, while the median year-end policy-rate forecast rose to 4.1%. President Trump has repeatedly called for rates of 1% or lower and criticized the Fed’s board, though he said he continued to support Chairman Kevin Warsh, whom he appointed. Warsh said the decision reflected the central bank’s assessment of inflation, employment and economic activity.
business.image_alt: Fed raises rates as Warsh signals further hikes

business.title: AI firms face growing scrutiny over risks from autonomous agents
business.summary: Artificial-intelligence companies face growing pressure to show how they control autonomous agents as the systems take on longer tasks, interact with other models and operate at speeds humans cannot easily review. The issue became especially visible in an incident involving nearly 12,000 agents at Hugging Face, where i
business.content: Artificial-intelligence companies face growing pressure to show how they control autonomous agents as the systems take on longer tasks, interact with other models and operate at speeds humans cannot easily review. The issue became especially visible in an incident involving nearly 12,000 agents at Hugging Face, where investigators used AI to process the volume. Lawmakers from both U.S. political parties are reportedly considering new rules, while efforts to regulate the industry have repeatedly stalled. Companies are deploying agent-reporting systems and AI-based observability tools, but researchers and investors disagree over whether AI can reliably control other AI systems.
business.image_alt: AI firms face growing scrutiny over risks from autonomous agents

business.title: AI leaders debate slowing frontier development at Dreamforce
business.summary: A debate over the pace of frontier artificial-intelligence development moved into the business spotlight at Salesforce’s Dreamforce conference in San Francisco, where OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang debated safety, innovation and the risks posed by increasingly capable AI s
business.content: A debate over the pace of frontier artificial-intelligence development moved into the business spotlight at Salesforce’s Dreamforce conference in San Francisco, where OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang debated safety, innovation and the risks posed by increasingly capable AI systems. Amodei’s September 12 essay, “We Must Pace the Frontier,” called for slowing improvements to the most advanced models. Altman and Elon Musk publicly backed the position, while Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis supported its direction but said the proposal needed more detail. Semiconductor shares declined during the week. VanEck said the SMH ETF fell 5.5% and SMHX fell 5.1% through September 15, while maintaining that no company had proposed a formal pause, spending cut or delay to a specific model. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg rejected a general slowdown, saying market incentives and legal liability would pressure companies to improve alignment.
business.image_alt: AI leaders debate slowing frontier development at Dreamforce

business.title: Barclays staff demand travel support over office mandate
business.summary: Thousands of Barclays employees are opposing the bank’s plan to require most staff to work from the office at least three days a week from October 2026, up from two days. Senior employees will be expected to attend at least four days a week. Unite, which represents about 36,000 workers, nearly 80% of Barclays’ 45,000 U
business.content: Thousands of Barclays employees are opposing the bank’s plan to require most staff to work from the office at least three days a week from October 2026, up from two days. Senior employees will be expected to attend at least four days a week. Unite, which represents about 36,000 workers, nearly 80% of Barclays’ 45,000 UK staff, is seeking exemptions for employees who live more than 40 minutes from work and payments to offset higher travel and childcare costs. The bank outlined the expectations in a July memo and said many employees already work onsite three or more days a week. Barclays said office attendance supports collaboration and peer learning, while recognising the need to balance workplace flexibility with working together in offices. Unite national officer Rick Coyle said thousands of workers had signed an open letter calling for the policy to be reversed and that the number was continuing to rise.
business.image_alt: Barclays staff demand travel support over office mandate

business.title: Record diesel prices threaten U.S. transport and consumer costs
business.summary: U.S. diesel prices have reached record highs as disruptions linked to the Iran conflict, the Russia-Ukraine war and refinery constraints limit fuel supplies. The national diesel average reached $6.40 a gallon on Sept. 17, up 77 cents since the start of September, while gasoline rose 7 cents overnight to $4.44, accordin
business.content: U.S. diesel prices have reached record highs as disruptions linked to the Iran conflict, the Russia-Ukraine war and refinery constraints limit fuel supplies. The national diesel average reached $6.40 a gallon on Sept. 17, up 77 cents since the start of September, while gasoline rose 7 cents overnight to $4.44, according to CBS News. Brent crude briefly approached $110 a barrel before easing to about $107, but economists said diesel and gasoline prices have a more direct effect on household and business costs than the $100 crude threshold. Diesel costs directly affect trucking, rail, construction, farming and freight distribution, making it harder for companies to absorb higher operating expenses without raising prices. Economists noted that gasoline accounts for about 2.5% of U.S. household income, compared with about 6% in 1980, while diesel remains essential to commercial activity. The national gasoline average could reach $4.50 within days, according to GasBuddy petroleum analyst Patrick De Haan.
business.image_alt: Record diesel prices threaten U.S. transport and consumer costs

business.title: Bank of England holds rates, signals hikes as inflation rises
business.summary: The Bank of England held its main interest rate at 3.75% on Thursday for a sixth consecutive meeting, warning that persistent energy-price volatility could require higher borrowing costs. The Monetary Policy Committee voted 6-3 to maintain the rate, with three members favoring a 0.25-percentage-point increase to 4%. UK
business.content: The Bank of England held its main interest rate at 3.75% on Thursday for a sixth consecutive meeting, warning that persistent energy-price volatility could require higher borrowing costs. The Monetary Policy Committee voted 6-3 to maintain the rate, with three members favoring a 0.25-percentage-point increase to 4%. UK consumer-price inflation rose to 3.1% in August from 2.9% in July, above the Bank’s 2% target. The Bank raised its inflation forecast to slightly above 4% early next year, citing higher fuel costs and an expected substantial increase in the January household energy-price cap. Governor Andrew Bailey said energy costs had so far had limited effects on wage and price setting, but prolonged volatility would increase the likelihood of a rate rise. The Bank also slowed sales of government bonds acquired through quantitative easing and announced a multiyear plan to unwind the asset-purchase facility.
business.image_alt: Bank of England holds rates, signals hikes as inflation rises

science.title: NASA marks 50 years since shuttle Enterprise rollout
science.summary: Enterprise, NASA’s first space shuttle, rolled out on Sept. 17, 1976, at the Rockwell plant in Palmdale, California. The orbiter, designated OV-101, was unveiled at a Constitution Day ceremony during the United States’ bicentennial year. NASA had planned to name the vehicle Constitution, but a campaign by Star Trek fan
science.content: Enterprise, NASA’s first space shuttle, rolled out on Sept. 17, 1976, at the Rockwell plant in Palmdale, California. The orbiter, designated OV-101, was unveiled at a Constitution Day ceremony during the United States’ bicentennial year. NASA had planned to name the vehicle Constitution, but a campaign by Star Trek fans helped persuade President Gerald Ford to name it Enterprise after the fictional spacecraft in the television series. About 600 invited guests, including members of the Star Trek cast, attended the rollout.
science.image_alt: NASA marks 50 years since shuttle Enterprise rollout

science.title: Kuwaiti photographer wins 2026 astronomy image competition
science.summary: Kuwaiti photographer Ali Alobaidly won the Royal Observatory Greenwich’s 2026 ZWO Astronomy Photographer of the Year competition with “The Quiet Predator,” an image of the Shark Nebula, also known as LDN 1235. The dark nebula lies about 650 light-years away in the constellation Cepheus and consists of interstellar dust
science.content: Kuwaiti photographer Ali Alobaidly won the Royal Observatory Greenwich’s 2026 ZWO Astronomy Photographer of the Year competition with “The Quiet Predator,” an image of the Shark Nebula, also known as LDN 1235. The dark nebula lies about 650 light-years away in the constellation Cepheus and consists of interstellar dust dense enough to block starlight. Its blue regions are reflection nebulae. Alobaidly captured the image in Kuwait’s Jahra Governorate over two nights in August 2025. Nearly 4,000 entries from 66 countries were submitted for the 18th annual competition, and the overall winner received £10,000. The accompanying exhibition opens at London’s National Maritime Museum on September 18, 2026.
science.image_alt: Kuwaiti photographer wins 2026 astronomy image competition

science.title: Astronomers confirm youngest known exoplanet Elias 2-24 b
science.summary: Astronomers have confirmed Elias 2-24 b, a Jupiter-mass exoplanet less than 1 million years old that orbits a newly formed star about 450 light-years from Earth. It is the youngest known planet and remains within the gas-and-dust disk from which it formed. Andrea Bernardi of Diego Portales University in Chile led the s
science.content: Astronomers have confirmed Elias 2-24 b, a Jupiter-mass exoplanet less than 1 million years old that orbits a newly formed star about 450 light-years from Earth. It is the youngest known planet and remains within the gas-and-dust disk from which it formed. Andrea Bernardi of Diego Portales University in Chile led the study, which was published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters on September 16, 2026.
science.image_alt: Astronomers confirm youngest known exoplanet Elias 2-24 b

science.title: Rare inherited gene raises lung cancer risk in nonsmokers
science.summary: Researchers have identified an inherited EGFR T790M mutation associated with a substantially higher risk of lung cancer, including among people who have never smoked. The study, published Sept. 17 in Science, analysed de-identified genetic data from more than 3.3 million 23andMe participants who consented to research a
science.content: Researchers have identified an inherited EGFR T790M mutation associated with a substantially higher risk of lung cancer, including among people who have never smoked. The study, published Sept. 17 in Science, analysed de-identified genetic data from more than 3.3 million 23andMe participants who consented to research and found that carriers had about 25 times the odds of developing lung cancer overall. Among never-smokers, the study found that carriers were 62 times more likely to develop lung cancer than noncarriers. The mutation was much more common among people born in Southern Appalachia and other southeastern U.S. states than elsewhere in the country. Researchers said the variant probably explains only a small share of lung-cancer cases in never-smokers, but its effect could be relevant to genetic testing and risk-based screening research.
science.image_alt: Rare inherited gene raises lung cancer risk in nonsmokers

science.title: Trump administration narrows nationwide endangered species protections
science.summary: The Trump administration has directed the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to stop treating the foreseeable, unintentional killing of protected wildlife as an unlawful “take” under the Endangered Species Act. A Sept. 14 directive signed by agency Director Brian Nesvik says prohibited conduct must intentionally target a p
science.content: The Trump administration has directed the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to stop treating the foreseeable, unintentional killing of protected wildlife as an unlawful “take” under the Endangered Species Act. A Sept. 14 directive signed by agency Director Brian Nesvik says prohibited conduct must intentionally target a particular animal or animals; the Interior Department confirmed the memo’s authenticity and said the directive implements a final rule rescinding the regulatory definition of “harm”. The interpretation could exempt deaths linked to commercial fishing, logging, construction, dams and vessel strikes if the activity does not specifically target an animal. The previous approach allowed liability for predictable accidental harm, including damage to grizzly bears, manatees and spotted owls. Conservation groups and former wildlife officials say the change removes incentives for mitigation and could affect species such as North Atlantic right whales, salmon, nesting bats and piping plovers; the administration says direct hunting, killing, wounding, capture and harassment remain prohibited.
science.image_alt: Trump administration narrows nationwide endangered species protections

science.title: Dust-driven chlorine chemistry alters ozone and methane levels
science.summary: A global chemistry-climate study found that mineral dust activates chlorine and iodine chemistry in the marine atmosphere, reducing tropospheric ozone over ocean regions. The mechanism helped explain ozone losses in dust-influenced areas that existing global models had not fully reproduced. A separate Science study con
science.content: A global chemistry-climate study found that mineral dust activates chlorine and iodine chemistry in the marine atmosphere, reducing tropospheric ozone over ocean regions. The mechanism helped explain ozone losses in dust-influenced areas that existing global models had not fully reproduced. A separate Science study concluded that dust-mediated chlorine chemistry shortened atmospheric methane’s lifetime during the Last Glacial Maximum, when dust concentrations were high. The studies identify dust-associated halogen reactions as part of atmospheric chemistry during modern dust events and past climate conditions.
science.image_alt: Dust-driven chlorine chemistry alters ozone and methane levels

science.title: El Niño and road expansion threaten Amazon rainforest
science.summary: Scientists warn that a strengthening El Niño, human-driven climate change and continued degradation could push the Amazon rainforest toward an irreversible ecological shift, potentially turning parts of the forest into savannah. The Amazon has already suffered severe degradation, and the current El Niño is described as
science.content: Scientists warn that a strengthening El Niño, human-driven climate change and continued degradation could push the Amazon rainforest toward an irreversible ecological shift, potentially turning parts of the forest into savannah. The Amazon has already suffered severe degradation, and the current El Niño is described as likely the strongest ever recorded, potentially intensifying drought pressure on the rainforest. A separate investigation examines Brazil’s BR-319, a 540-mile dirt highway linking Amazonas state to the rest of Brazil through a largely intact section of rainforest. Paving proposals have faced court challenges for decades and opposition from environmental groups and regulators; researchers and conservationists warn that improved access could accelerate forest destruction and increase climate risks.
science.image_alt: El Niño and road expansion threaten Amazon rainforest

science.title: Simulations link Webb’s Little Red Dots to black holes
science.summary: Japanese researchers used the ATERUI III supercomputer to model the early universe and found that Webb’s “Little Red Dots” could be rapidly growing black holes. The simulations produced compact, intensely red objects resembling those observed by the James Webb Space Telescope without requiring exotic physics. The model
science.content: Japanese researchers used the ATERUI III supercomputer to model the early universe and found that Webb’s “Little Red Dots” could be rapidly growing black holes. The simulations produced compact, intensely red objects resembling those observed by the James Webb Space Telescope without requiring exotic physics. The model proposes that strong ultraviolet radiation in young galaxies prevented dense gas clouds from fragmenting into ordinary stellar nurseries. Instead, some clouds collapsed into unusually massive black-hole seeds, and abundant surrounding gas allowed them to grow dozens of times faster than black holes can today. The interpretation is one explanation for the objects’ nature; astronomers have also considered other possibilities, including massive progenitor stars.
science.image_alt: Simulations link Webb’s Little Red Dots to black holes

sports.title: US coach Pochettino names youthful roster for friendlies
sports.summary: United States coach Mauricio Pochettino has named a 28-player roster for four post-World Cup friendlies against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada as the team begins its 2030 World Cup cycle. The roster includes 13 uncapped players, while Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie are among the notable absences
sports.content: United States coach Mauricio Pochettino has named a 28-player roster for four post-World Cup friendlies against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada as the team begins its 2030 World Cup cycle. The roster includes 13 uncapped players, while Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie are among the notable absences. Pulisic recently returned to AC Milan after sustaining a bone bruise and microfracture in his lower leg during the World Cup. Philadelphia Union's 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan is among the newcomers. Eight of the uncapped selections are teenagers, and the roster averages 22 years and nine months, more than four years younger than the World Cup squad. The United States will play Peru in Orlando on September 26, Chile in St. Louis on September 29, Mexico in the Phoenix area on October 3 and Canada in St. Paul on October 6.
sports.image_alt: US coach Pochettino names youthful roster for friendlies

sports.title: Australian Hyrox athlete forfeits Beijing victory after apology
sports.summary: Australian Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk has apologised for continuing a Beijing race after suffering sudden fecal incontinence. She has withdrawn from the event, forfeiting the victory and points she earned. Wietrzyk said she felt fit and healthy before the women’s competition on September 12 and had no reason to expe
sports.content: Australian Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk has apologised for continuing a Beijing race after suffering sudden fecal incontinence. She has withdrawn from the event, forfeiting the victory and points she earned. Wietrzyk said she felt fit and healthy before the women’s competition on September 12 and had no reason to expect illness, but later acknowledged that she should have left the track. The incident drew criticism because she continued using shared mats and equipment while Hyrox officials allowed the race to continue.
sports.image_alt: Australian Hyrox athlete forfeits Beijing victory after apology

sports.title: Arsenal target Bournemouth forward Kroupi for January move
sports.summary: Arsenal are considering a January move for Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi. The 20-year-old France Under-21 international has emerged as an attacking target. Kroupi scored 13 Premier League goals last season but has not played this campaign following foot surgery. Bournemouth are understood to value Kroupi at abo
sports.content: Arsenal are considering a January move for Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi. The 20-year-old France Under-21 international has emerged as an attacking target. Kroupi scored 13 Premier League goals last season but has not played this campaign following foot surgery. Bournemouth are understood to value Kroupi at about £100 million. Arsenal's interest partly depends on Kroupi's recovery from a pre-season foot injury expected to keep him out for three to four months.
sports.image_alt: Arsenal target Bournemouth forward Kroupi for January move

sports.title: England seal T20 series against Sri Lanka in Cardiff
sports.summary: England beat Sri Lanka by six wickets in Cardiff on 17 September, taking an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match T20 series with one match remaining. Tom Banton’s unbeaten 52 off 24 balls led England’s chase.

sports.content: Ferencvaros beat Celtic 3-1 at Celtic Park on Thursday in Celtic’s Europa League league-phase opener. Bamidele Yusuf’s deflected effort put the visitors ahead in the 20th minute, Mika Baur equalised in the 44th, and Kristoffer Zachariassen restored Ferencvaros’ lead before half-time. Former Celtic forward Daniel Arzani then struck from 20 yards two minutes after the restart. The defeat followed Celtic’s 3-0 League Cup loss to Rangers on Sunday, leaving manager Martin O’Neill facing another Old Firm meeting at Celtic Park on Sunday, September 20. O’Neill made four changes for the European match, recalling goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo and starting James Forrest, but Celtic again made defensive errors and failed to turn possession into sustained chances.

sports.content: Aaron Rai and Joakim Lagergren share the first-round lead at the BMW PGA Championship after shooting six-under-par 66s at Wentworth on Thursday, September 17. Rai made seven birdies and one bogey, while Lagergren’s round included an eagle and five birdies. Ryan Gerard, Adam Scott, Ludvig Aberg and Nacho Elvira sit one shot back on 67. Rory McIlroy started strongly and reached five under through 10 holes, but three bogeys over his final six left him on 69, three shots behind the leaders. The Northern Irishman called his finish a “stumble home” and said his putting had improved after last week’s Irish Open. McIlroy is pursuing a second BMW PGA Championship victory and a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title.

sports.title: Josh Allen leads Bills past Lions in stadium opener
sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills opened the regular season at their new Highmark Stadium with a 41-31 victory over the Detroit Lions in Orchard Park, New York, on Thursday, September 17. sports.content: The Buffalo Bills opened the regular season at their new Highmark Stadium with a 41-31 victory over the Detroit Lions in Orchard Park, New York, on Thursday, September 17. Josh Allen threw three touchdown passes and ran for two more, helping Buffalo build an early 21-0 lead and improve to 2-0 under first-year head coach Joe Brady. Detroit fell to 1-1 despite a second-half rally led by Jared Goff and Amon-Ra St. Brown. Allen completed 20 of 31 passes for 248 yards and added 69 rushing yards, while James Cook ran for 135 yards and a touchdown. Buffalo scored on its first four possessions, converted all five red-zone opportunities and held off Detroit after the Lions twice cut the deficit to 10 points. The $2.1 billion venue hosted a sellout crowd, fireworks and performances of the U.S. and Canadian national anthems.

sports.content: New York Mets first baseman Jared Young was taken to a hospital after colliding with teammate Nolan McLean during the sixth inning of Thursday’s 3-0 loss to the Philadelphia Phillies at Citi Field. Young was fielding a slow grounder hit by Phillies outfielder Justin Crawford as McLean moved toward first base. McLean’s knee struck Young’s head, leaving him motionless before medical personnel attended to him and carted him off the field. Interim manager Andy Green said Young’s CT scan was negative, he had full use of his extremities and was experiencing concussion symptoms. Young gave the crowd a thumbs-up as he was taken from the field.
